summary: October PPI actual is now published: headline +0.3% month-on-month versus +0.4% consensus, +6.5% year-on-year versus +6.6% forecast (but up from September's 6.3%). Post-release Nasdaq-100 futures were reported +0.5%, and Treasury yields edged lower. This is a modest near-term relief catalyst but not sufficient to reverse the existing Bearish — Elevated Downside Risk three-session base case without cash-market QQQ/SOX, breadth and volatility confirmation. Post-PPI reported 10Y 5.127% and 2Y 4.836% imply +29.1bp, correctly scaled. Open Watch remains 163 curated events. Core PPI details conflict across secondary reports and are not treated as verified.
bullish: October headline PPI +0.3% month-on-month undershot +0.4% consensus; +6.5% year-on-year undershot +6.6% consensus.
Barron's reported Nasdaq-100 futures +0.5% after the release; a favorable early response, not a confirmed regular-session trend.
WSJ reported post-PPI Treasury yields eased to 10Y 5.127% and 2Y 4.836%, supportive of duration-sensitive technology valuations.
Thursday AMD +5.86% and AVGO +5.54% closing gains and AMAT/Cisco earnings show selective AI infrastructure strength.
bearish: PPI year-over-year +6.5% still accelerated from September's +6.3%, so inflation pressure remains elevated despite the modest consensus undershoot.
Thursday NVDA -4.34% and SOX -0.54% show semiconductor leadership fragility; no confirmed Friday SOX recovery yet.
10Y yield near 5.13% remains a substantial growth-equity valuation headwind even after the reported decline.
No synchronized Friday QQQ/SOX breadth, VXN/VIX or verified live CME FedWatch to validate a sustained reversal.

editorial.marketOverview: Friday's October producer inflation release delivered modest relief against consensus: headline PPI rose 0.3% month-on-month versus 0.4% expected and 6.5% year-on-year versus 6.6% expected. Nevertheless annual wholesale inflation accelerated from September's 6.3%. Nasdaq-100 futures were reported up about 0.5% after the release and Treasury yields eased. The combination improves the immediate opening setup but does not erase Thursday's NVDA-led semiconductor fragility or high absolute interest-rate levels.
editorial.whatChanged: The prior 08:20 EST assessment had October PPI pending. At 08:30 EST the actual headline result became available and was marginally cooler than expected. Post-release WSJ quotes put the 10Y at 5.127% and 2Y at 4.836%, implying +29.1bp, while Barron's described Nasdaq-100 futures +0.5%. These are distinct reported observations, not a synchronized tick-level response. The curated Open Watch feed remains at 163 events. Conflicting secondary accounts of core PPI prevent a reliable core interpretation.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The surprise favors a tactical relief rally but does not establish a new three-day bullish regime. Year-on-year PPI remains elevated, yields remain above 5% at the long end, and the Nasdaq still needs semiconductor breadth and Nvidia leadership confirmation. A post-release futures bounce is evidence of initial optimism, not proof of a durable cash-session repricing.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday November 13 is now an observed PPI-relief opening setup rather than a pending binary inflation event. The decisive test is whether QQQ and SOX hold gains through the cash session with broader participation and stable volatility. Monday November 16 should reveal whether the reaction persists beyond the release. Tuesday November 17 introduces another inflation-linked import/export price checkpoint and potential AI earnings anticipation. The base case remains volatile, downside-skewed consolidation, with a credible but unconfirmed rebound scenario.
editorial.bullCase: If the cooler-than-consensus headline PPI translates into sustained lower yields and QQQ/SOX relative strength, Friday's relief could extend into Monday. NVDA stabilization, broad participation, contained VXN/VIX and resilient AMAT/AMD/AVGO leadership would argue for reducing the bearish skew. Confirmation requires regular-session observations, not just futures.
editorial.bearCase: If traders focus on the still-elevated 6.5% annual PPI or a firmer underlying inflation component, Treasury yields could rebound and the Nasdaq futures bounce could fade. Renewed Nvidia weakness, SOX underperformance, rising volatility or weak breadth would restore downside momentum into Monday and Tuesday. A stronger oil bid would add inflation pressure, but no fresh synchronized oil data is available.
editorial.watchNext: Verify official BLS detailed PPI and resolve conflicting core reports. At and after the cash open, capture timestamp-matched QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, NVDA, breadth, VXN/VIX, 2Y/10Y, Brent/WTI and CME FedWatch observations. Distinguish actual market reaction from projected catalyst impact. Check for new Open Watch events and independently confirm any earnings dates.
